scope: B2B dehydrated-fruit launch from Poranki, prioritizing cafes and cocktail bars
demand_limit: These are public menu and business-fit signals, not purchasing records, sales volumes, confirmed demand, or commitments to buy. No source establishes which dehydrated fruit sells most in Poranki or Vijayawada. The ranking below is a recommended order for customer trials, not a measured market-share ranking.
recommended_start: Start customer validation with orange wheels and lemon wheels; make lime a separate buyer-requested variant. Add pineapple only after a cafe or bar approves a tropical-drink use case. Test apple or mango with a specific bakery, breakfast-bowl or snack buyer before building stock. Dried garnishes do not replace fresh citrus juice, fresh muddled fruit or fruit puree in recipes.

trial_priority_by_fruit.strongest_customer_fit: Cocktail bars, restobars and beverage-focused cafes
trial_priority_by_fruit.reasoning: A regional hotel restaurant explicitly lists dehydrated orange in a cocktail, providing a concrete existing format to demonstrate. Broader fit to citrus drinks is an inference that must be tested venue by venue.
trial_priority_by_fruit.ask_buyer: Which drinks could use an orange wheel? What diameter, color, peel bitterness, pack size and cost per usable wheel do you accept? Do you currently buy or dry it yourself?

trial_priority_by_fruit.fruit: Lemon; lime as a separately specified variant
trial_priority_by_fruit.strongest_customer_fit: Iced-tea and mocktail cafes; bars serving citrus drinks
trial_priority_by_fruit.reasoning: Primary menus show citrus, lemon and lime drink ingredients. This supports a garnish trial but does not prove a need for dried wheels. Fermented black lime is a different product and should not be substituted with ordinary dried lime.
trial_priority_by_fruit.ask_buyer: Do you want lemon or lime, which local variety and wheel size, and is the garnish decorative or expected to add flavor? Test appearance and bitterness in the actual drink.

trial_priority_by_fruit.launch_role: Second-stage sample after confirmed tropical-drink fit
trial_priority_by_fruit.strongest_customer_fit: Tropical cocktail/mocktail cafes and selected dessert kitchens
trial_priority_by_fruit.reasoning: Primary bar menus include pineapple, so a dried pineapple garnish can be proposed. Fresh pineapple, juice and clarified pineapple are distinct ingredients; those menu mentions alone do not establish dried-pineapple demand.
trial_priority_by_fruit.ask_buyer: Would you prefer a thin decorative piece or a chewy edible piece? How many relevant drinks are sold weekly? Test breakage and texture in their serving format.

trial_priority_by_fruit.reasoning: A primary cafe menu demonstrates a granola-and-yogurt use case, but no verified apple-drying purchase demand was found. Dried apple is a proposed addition rather than a substitution automatically implied by fresh-fruit menus.
trial_priority_by_fruit.ask_buyer: Does the kitchen want slices, small dice or a snack? Confirm desired chew/crunch and color; trial any pretreatment and declare ingredients accurately.

trial_priority_by_fruit.strongest_customer_fit: Selected bakeries, bowl cafes and packaged-snack buyers
trial_priority_by_fruit.reasoning: Primary menus feature mango-flavored drinks and a cafe offers healthy-snack categories. This is evidence of flavor familiarity, not proof that dehydrated mango will fit those recipes. Validate a distinct strip/dice product with a buyer first.
trial_priority_by_fruit.ask_buyer: Do you need an unsweetened snack strip, diced inclusion or garnish? Is the accepted texture chewy or crisp? Confirm acceptance of color variation and the exact ingredient specification.

priority_by_business_type.first_offer: Orange, then lemon/lime; pineapple where tropical drinks exist
priority_by_business_type.proof_to_collect: Current garnish process, acceptable cost per usable piece, relevant drink sales, in-house drying cost, sample acceptance and paid reorder.

priority_by_business_type.first_offer: Lemon and orange; pineapple for an approved tropical drink
priority_by_business_type.proof_to_collect: Which exact drink will use the garnish, willingness to pay for it, presentation benefit and repeat weekly use.

priority_by_business_type.first_offer: Orange decoration; small apple, pineapple or mango inclusion trials
priority_by_business_type.proof_to_collect: Approved recipe trial, moisture/texture specification, ingredient declaration and purchase quantity.

priority_by_business_type.first_offer: Apple or mango samples matched to the actual menu
priority_by_business_type.proof_to_collect: Whether a dried topping is wanted at all, acceptable chew/crunch, serving size and paid reorder.

priority_by_business_type.business_type: Basic bars with limited cocktail service
priority_by_business_type.proof_to_collect: Existence of a cocktail or mocktail menu and a buyer willing to pay for presentation garnishes. Alcohol service alone does not imply dried-fruit demand.

commercial_validation_steps: Visit nearby Poranki and Vijayawada prospects first and ask which exact drinks or foods could use a sample. Treat an unqualified contact as a lead, not a customer.
Use small, clearly labeled trials to compare appearance, aroma, bitterness, texture, breakage, pack resealing and consistency in the buyer's actual recipe.
Record paid sample/trial results and repeat orders; select the first production range from those results instead of treating menu mentions as demand volumes.
Before choosing equipment capacity, measure wet fruit input, usable dry output, usable pieces, rejects, preparation time, electricity, packaging and freight on representative batches.
Price garnish packs using cost per usable piece as well as net weight. Do not estimate an order from the venue's total covers without asking about relevant drinks.
equipment_and_quality_implications: For a pilot machine, compare adjustable temperature control, forced airflow, timer, cleanable food-contact trays, service support and real usable tray area. Request a demonstration with the fruit and slice size you plan to sell. Tray count or advertised wet-load capacity is not a finished-product capacity guarantee.
Use uniform preparation and control temperature, airflow and humidity. Test multiple tray positions rather than relying only on an elapsed drying time.

Cool product appropriately before packing and select food-contact packaging that limits moisture entry. Smaller use-size packs may suit bar service because opening repeatedly exposes product to humid air.

Validate the commercial process, finished product, packaging and intended storage conditions with a qualified food technologist/laboratory. Check water activity, applicable microbiological/product requirements and a supported shelf-life specification.

Do not copy the shelf-life durations from home-preservation articles onto a commercial label. Crisp appearance, final weight, vacuum sealing or meeting a moisture figure alone is not a commercial shelf-life study.
The cited extension resources explain general drying principles; they do not replace Indian food-business registration, product standards, labeling or commercial process validation.

sources.title: Lush Bengaluru official menus
sources.facts: The Highlander cocktail lists dehydrated orange. Other drinks list fresh citrus or fruit components.
sources.implication: Direct evidence that dehydrated orange is used in at least one South Indian venue's published menu. It does not show supplier availability, purchase volume, profitability or demand in Poranki.

sources.title: Mirth Bengaluru official cocktail list
sources.source_type: Primary business menu, visible in official-domain search index
sources.facts: Cocktails feature lime, lemon, pineapple/citrus and mango tea in different recipes.
sources.implication: These flavor cues identify questions for a bar-manager tasting. Dried forms and supplier demand are not stated. Direct retrieval timed out; confirm the current menu before a personalized pitch.

sources.title: Sundays Chennai beverage program
sources.facts: Site describes spritzes, Old Fashioneds and zero-alcohol drinks, and a conceptual cocktail menu featuring fermented black lime.
sources.implication: A beverage-led venue is a plausible garnish prospect. Fermented black lime and ordinary dehydrated lime wheels are different products, and no purchase demand for the latter is confirmed.

sources.title: Pandhal Cafe & Deli official menu
sources.facts: The Power Bowl combines granola, coconut yogurt, nuts and fresh fruit; the cafe also offers desserts.
sources.implication: Possible channel for a chef-approved dried-fruit topping experiment. Existing fresh-fruit ingredients are not evidence that dried apple or mango is already wanted.

sources.title: Fresh Choice official site
sources.source_type: Primary business menu and product categories
sources.facts: Site lists pastries, beverages and healthy snacks, and features Mango Chilli Soda.
sources.implication: Useful bakery/cafe prospect and mango-flavor cue. Dehydrated mango remains a proposed new application rather than a confirmed ingredient requirement.

sources.title: National Center for Home Food Preservation: Food Dehydrators
sources.facts: Describes heat, airflow and vents; recommends features such as temperature adjustment, fan and timer. Explains more even tray heating and reduced flavor mixing as benefits of horizontal airflow.
sources.implication: Use these as machine-comparison criteria, alongside a trial with the intended fruit and local service support. The article covers home equipment and does not validate a commercial machine's throughput.

sources.title: National Center for Home Food Preservation: Packaging and Storing Dried Foods
sources.facts: Dried food can absorb moisture again. Packing warm food can cause condensation; repeated package opening introduces air and moisture. Fruit conditioning equalizes remaining moisture in home-dried pieces.
sources.implication: Cooling, moisture-resistant sealed packaging and pack size deserve testing. Home conditioning guidance and suggested household storage times do not establish a commercial shelf-life claim.

sources.title: FDA: Water Activity in Foods
sources.facts: Water activity describes water availability and affects microbial stability. Some water is bound within food; temperature control matters when measuring water activity.
sources.implication: A batch's weight loss or total moisture does not by itself establish its water activity or safe shelf life. Seek product-appropriate laboratory validation; this US technical reference is not an Indian licensing rule.

sources.title: Montana State University Extension: Drying Fruits
sources.facts: Fruit quality and ripeness affect the dried result. Pretreatment is recommended for quality; tray crowding, scorching, cooling and moisture re-entry matter. Dried fruit texture varies by fruit and may remain flexible.
sources.implication: Use buyer-approved fruit varieties and repeatable preparation. Do not promise freeze-dried-like crunch from a small hot-air dryer; assess the actual finished texture and ingredients.

sources.title: National Center for Home Food Preservation: Sun Drying
sources.facts: Outdoor drying depends on sufficiently dry, warm, moving air, takes multiple days and can be affected by rain or overnight condensation.
sources.implication: A controlled indoor dehydrator is a more repeatable pilot choice than weather-dependent outdoor drying. This is an equipment-planning inference, not a local climatic measurement.
